skills.name: Areas and volumes of similar figures

sections.heading: Why areas grow faster
sections.text:
Double every length of a {1} cm square: it becomes {2} cm by {2} cm, and its area goes from {1} cm² to {4} cm².
Area is length × length, so a length factor k gives an area factor k × k = k².
For k = {3}, areas are multiplied by {9}. A floor plan drawn three times larger needs nine times as much paper.

sections.heading: And volumes faster still
sections.text:
Volume is length × length × length, so the volume factor is k³.
Double the sides of a cube: the volume is multiplied by {8}. A tin twice as tall (and similar) holds eight times as much.
Objects made of the same material have mass proportional to volume, so masses also go up by k³.

sections.heading: Working backwards
sections.text:
If you know the ratio of areas, take square roots to get the length ratio: areas {16} : {25} → lengths {4} : {5}.
If you know the ratio of volumes, take cube roots: volumes {8} : {125} → lengths {2} : {5}.
Then use the length ratio to find whatever you need.

mistake.wrong: Lengths doubled, so the area is doubled
mistake.why: Area uses two lengths, so the factor is applied twice.

worked_example.problem: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides {2} cm and {2 * k} cm. The smaller has area {A} cm². Find the area of the larger.
steps: Larger area = {k * k} × {A} = {k * k * A} cm².

check.prompt: Two similar tins of tomato paste have heights {h} cm and {h * k} cm. The small tin holds {V} cm³. How much does the large tin hold (cm³)?

misconceptions.explain: k² is for areas; volumes use k³.

cards.idea: From an area ratio, take square roots to get the length ratio.

check.prompt: Two similar figures have areas {a * a * m} cm² and {b * b * m} cm². The smaller has a side of {a * n} cm. Find the matching side of the larger (cm).

misconceptions.explain: The area ratio is k²: take the square root to get the length ratio.

solution: Area ratio {a * a * m} : {b * b * m} = {a * a} : {b * b}.
where: a * n * b * b / (a * a) != b * n

questions.prompt: Two similar shapes have linear scale factor {k}. The smaller has area {A} cm². Find the area of the larger (cm²).

misconceptions.explain: Areas use k², not k: {k} × {k} = {k * k}.
k³ is for volumes; areas use k².

questions.prompt: Two similar tins of tomato paste have heights {h} cm and {h * k} cm. The small tin holds {V} cm³. How much does the large tin hold (cm³)?

misconceptions.explain: k² is for areas; volumes use k³.

questions.prompt: Two similar figures have areas {a * a * m} cm² and {b * b * m} cm². The smaller has a side of {a * n} cm. Find the matching side of the larger (cm).

misconceptions.explain: The area ratio is k²: take the square root to get the length ratio.

solution: Area ratio {a * a * m} : {b * b * m} = {a * a} : {b * b}.
where: a * n * b * b / (a * a) != b * n

questions.prompt: Two similar statues are made of the same wood. Their heights are {p} cm and {q} cm. The small one has mass {M} g. Find the mass of the large one (g).
questions.answer: M * q * q * q / (p * p * p)

misconceptions.explain: Mass goes with volume: use k³, not k.

solution: Mass is proportional to volume: factor k³.
Mass = {M} × {q * q * q} ÷ {p * p * p} = {answer} g.

questions.prompt: Two similar jugs have volumes {a * a * a} litres and {b * b * b} litres. The surface area of the small jug is {A} cm². Find the surface area of the large jug (cm²).

misconceptions.wrong: A * b * b * b / (a * a * a)
misconceptions.explain: Areas use k², not k³: first find k from the cube root.

solution: Volume ratio = k³ = {b * b * b} ÷ {a * a * a}, so k = {b} ÷ {a} (cube root).
